item.title: JPY/USD: Why Yen Intervention by Japan and US Has Limited Impact
item.description: The yen’s weakness has become a growing issue for Japan’s policymakers, given its role in driving up import prices and household living costs. It’s also become a worry for the US.

item.title: IEA Sees Wider Oil Supply Deficit Despite Hit to Demand From War
item.description: Global oil inventories will tumble this quarter at more than twice the rate previously estimated as the Iran war flares again, even as the hit to demand from high prices deepens, the International Energy Agency said.

item.title: Machinery Maker DMG Mori Seeks $300 Million in Japan Share Sale
item.description: DMG Mori Co. is aiming to raise ¥48.2 billion ($302 million) through the sale of new shares in the overseas markets as global investors show solid appetite for the nation’s stocks.

item.title: Ex-Alibaba AI Architect Wins Tencent, HSG Backing for New Lab
item.description: The former architect of Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s flagship model has founded a startup to build AI agents, securing backing from Tencent Holdings Ltd. and Chinese venture heavyweights.

item.title: Russian Economy Poised to Resume Growth Despite Drone Strikes
item.description: Russia’s economy likely grew in the second quarter after its first contraction in three years, but an escalating wave of Ukrainian drone attacks deep inside the country threatens to derail the fragile recovery.

item.title: UAE Shuttles Oil Exports From Iraq Through the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. is offering to shuttle exports of Iraqi oil through the Strait of Hormuz, using its dark-transit playbook to transport Basrah and other crude to refiners in Asia, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Shoprite Jumps as E-Commerce Boom Boosts Full-Year Profit
item.description: Shoprite Holdings Ltd. climbed the most in 11 months as Africa’s largest supermarket chain said it sees earnings rising as much as 14.7% because of higher sales at its e-commerce unit.

item.title: Nvidia Partner Hon Hai’s Profit Beats on Sustained AI Spending
item.description: Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. reported a better-than-expected increase in quarterly profit, signaling robust global demand for AI hardware.

item.title: China Pledge on US Soybeans Tested as Private Crushers Hold Back
item.description: China’s drive to buy large volumes of US soybeans — a commitment under last year’s trade truce — risks being complicated by a lack of participation from the country’s private traders.

item.title: Norway $2.3 Trillion Fund Posts Best Quarter Since 2020
item.description: Norway’s sovereign wealth fund, the world’s largest, reported its best quarterly return in six years, helped by gains from its large holdings in global technology companies.

item.title: Activist Elliott Names Candidates for Board of Northern Star
item.description: Activist investor Elliott Investment Management LP has nominated six candidates for the board of Australia’s biggest gold miner Northern Star Resources Ltd., stepping up its campaign to improve the company’s performance.

item.title: India Options Trading Drops 27% as New Auction Upends Strategies
item.description: Index-options trading volumes in India have slumped in the first week of the new closing auction mechanism as traders adjust to one of the country’s biggest market-structure overhauls in years.

item.title: FTSE 100 Live: UK Stocks Set to Fall Again, Pound Holds Steady
item.description: FTSE 100 Live: UK Stocks Set to Fall Again, Pound Holds Steady【原文：FTSE 100 Live: UK Stocks Set to Fall Again, Pound Holds Steady】

item.title: Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran Resigns Ahead of AGM Next Week
item.description: Natarajan Chandrasekaran has stepped down as chairman of Tata Sons Pvt. ahead of a contentious annual shareholder vote, according to a person familiar with the matter, throwing the salt-to-software conglomerate into uncertainty at a time when it’s spearheading the country’s push into high-tech sectors.

item.title: ABN Amro Beats on Profit, Boosts Key Revenue Source Outlook
item.description: ABN Amro Bank NV reported quarterly profit that beat analysts’ estimates thanks to higher fees and growth in lending income, prompting the Dutch bank to raise the outlook for its biggest revenue source.

item.title: Godrej Consumer Shares Plunge After CEO’s Sudden Resignation
item.description: Godrej Consumer Products Ltd. shares fell after the Indian soap and mosquito-repellent maker said its Chief Executive Officer Sudhir Sitapati resigned with immediate effect, surprising market watchers.

item.title: Vacuum Pump Makers, Producers of Gases Are the New AI Winners
item.description: European makers of vacuum pumps, heat exchangers and specialty gases are cementing their spot as lesser-known winners of the artificial-intelligence boom, creating new opportunities for investors wary of more established AI stocks.

item.title: AGL Jumps Most in Six Months on Strong Battery Performance
item.description: AGL Energy Ltd. shares jumped the most in six months as Australia’s largest power producer’s batteries helped offset declining wholesale electricity prices.

item.title: Qatar National Bank Tests Investor Appetite for $2 Billion Loan
item.description: Qatar National Bank is seeking a $2 billion syndicated loan, according to people familiar with the matter, in a test of whether banks, particularly from Asia, are willing to lend in the region as the US war with Iran drags on.

item.title: AI Startup Cognition in New Funding Talks at $40 Billion Value
item.description: Cognition AI is in early talks with investors for a new funding round that may boost the coding startup’s valuation by more than 50% to at least $40 billion, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: JPMorgan Boosts Singapore Stocks Target as Economic Growth Holds
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. raised its target for Singapore stocks as robust economic growth and a narrowing valuation gap with developed-market peers bolster their outlook.

item.title: Indonesian Tech Firm GoTo Faces MSCI Index Exclusion in Review
item.description: GoTo Group, the Indonesian ride-hailing and food delivery platform once valued at more than $32 billion, faces the prospect of being dropped from MSCI Inc.’s indexes on Wednesday after a plunge in its share price left the stock difficult to trade.

item.title: SK Hynix, Samsung Shares Rally as Temasek Report Boosts Optimism
item.description: South Korean chipmakers rallied as risk appetite returns after last month’s rout, with a local media report of investment plans by Singapore’s Temasek Holdings Pte supporting sentiment.

item.title: China Taps Deutsche Bank as First Foreign Yuan Clearer in Europe
item.description: China has authorized Deutsche Bank AG as the first non-Chinese lender that can settle yuan transactions in Europe, expanding its clearing network to promote the currency overseas.

item.title: Korea’s 30-Year Bond Yield Hits Record on Oil, Rate Hike Bets
item.description: South Korea’s 30-year government bond yield climbed to a record, as elevated energy prices and weaker demand from life insurers intensified pressure on the debt market.

item.title: Bessent-Takaichi Split on BOJ Risks Undermining Joint Yen Rescue
item.description: Even as the US and Japan have shown rare unity in moving to strengthen the yen, a fundamental tension between Scott Bessent and Sanae Takaichi over the Bank of Japan risks undermining their efforts.

item.title: India’s Small, Mid-cap Funds Stay Hot With Investors
item.description: The smaller stocks have comfortably outpaced large caps this year.

item.title: Yen Traders Use Options for ‘Flexibility’ Into US Inflation Data
item.description: Yen traders are ramping up options market activity ahead of key US inflation data, turning to derivatives for flexibility amid a lack of consensus on the currency’s direction.

item.title: Sanrio Shares Plunge Most Since 2014 After 1Q Earnings Miss
item.description: Sanrio Co. shares tumbled as much as 20%, the most in more than 12 years, after the company’s first quarter operating income missed market estimates.

item.title: China Revives Free-Trade Zone Bond Market After 2023 Crackdown
item.description: Signs of life are returning to the Shanghai free-trade zone’s bond market, which went quiet in late 2023 after Chinese authorities clamped down on excessive borrowing by local governments.
